caption: The drawing depicts a baptismal font table from San Buenaventura, dated 1809. The main object is a pedestal-like structure with a wide, flat top and a base that flares outward. The body of the table has curved sides and is predominantly a light reddish-brown color with shading and highlights in white, beige, and gray. The front of the pedestal features a circular design in the center, which contains a stylized sunburst pattern with red rays and a central red circle, all surrounded by a plain white ring and an outer gray border. The top and bottom edges of the pedestal have additional horizontal bands in beige and gray. Written notes and measurements surround the drawing, including dimensions for various parts of the table and a horizontal scale of 3 inches to 1 foot in the lower left. Beneath the pedestal, there are detailed measurement diagrams showing widths, base depth, and other statistics. The drawing appears to be rendered in watercolor and ink, giving soft shading and clear, precise lines. The upper part of the page contains handwritten text identifying the object and its historical context. The artist's name, Dayton Brown, is written at the right edge.
title: Stand for Baptismal Font
